style: Greasy psychedelic funk duet, 100 BPM, exactly two singers and no others. HIM: a laid-back London geezer, dry wit, warm low voice, glottal stops, cool half-spoken half-sung patter on every verse, never rapped, unbothered, then bursting into excited gospel-soul shouts when he answers her. HER: a classical operatic mezzo-soprano diva, full bel canto, rich vibrato, grand and theatrical, singing the hook lines like an aria. Tight funk band: fuzz guitar riffs, wah rhythm guitar, greasy Hammond organ, congas, round fingered bass, crisp dry drums. Spaghetti-western colour: a mariachi-style trumpet and a lone whistled melody in the intro and between hooks. Clean, dry studio room, close mics, no echo tails, every instrument distinct
exclude: crowd, gang vocals, choir, chanting crowd, backing singers, dub, echo, delay throws, heavy reverb, screaming, trap, double-time, fast rap, rap, hip hop, boom bap, autotune, EDM, country, smooth R&B, American accent, comedy, novelty, kazoo, sitar, drone, dancehall, reggaeton
